# Nova Browser - Complete Technical Specification & Documentation

## 1. Overview
Nova Browser is an open-source, AI-native desktop web browser built with Electron, React 19, Tailwind CSS v4, WebGPU, and Rust-based network filtering. It is designed to provide sovereign, high-speed, and completely private web browsing with local AI capabilities.

## 2. Core Architecture & Philosophy

### 2.1 Sovereign On-Device AI Engine
- **Inference Technology**: Uses WebGPU hardware shaders to execute quantized Large Language Models (GGUF / MLC format) directly on client hardware (Metal on macOS, DirectX 12 / Vulkan on Windows).
- **Supported Models**:
  - Llama 3.2 3B Instruct (General reasoning, code analysis, document summarization)
  - Phi-3.5 Vision Instruct (Visual screenshot analysis and multimodal UI understanding)
  - Qwen 2.5 1.5B (Ultra-fast lightweight execution on lower-spec hardware)
- **Data Privacy**: Zero prompts, history, or tokens leave the user device. 100% offline-capable.

### 2.2 Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration
- Nova features a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server running on `localhost:3020`.
- External AI clients (such as Claude Desktop, Cursor IDE, Antigravity, or custom local agents) can connect via SSE (Server-Sent Events) and control browser actions with granular permissions:
  - `browser_navigate`: Navigate to any URL
  - `browser_read_page`: Extract clean sanitized markdown text and link trees
  - `browser_screenshot`: Capture viewport or element screenshots
  - `browser_list_tabs`, `browser_switch_tab`, `browser_close_tab`, `browser_new_tab`
  - `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_hover`

### 2.3 Zero-Latency Privacy & Ad-Blocker Engine
- Integrates memory-mapped EasyList, EasyPrivacy, uBlock Origin, and Peter Lowe blocklists.
- Stops cross-site trackers, crypto-miners, fingerprinting scripts, and intrusive banners before network dispatch.
- Enforces strict Global Privacy Control (Sec-GPC) and Do-Not-Track (DNT) headers.

### 2.4 Zero-Knowledge Cloud Sync (Nova Sync)
- Synchronization of open tabs, workspaces, speed dials, bookmarks, and settings.
- Uses client-side AES-256-GCM encryption with ephemeral device pairing codes.
- The cloud backend (Supabase Realtime) only stores blinded ciphertext payloads, ensuring zero-knowledge privacy.

## 3. Platform Availability & Installation

### macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel)
- Homebrew Cask (Recommended):
  ```bash
  brew tap unitybtw/tap
  brew install --cask nova-browser
  ```
- Direct DMG Downloads:
  - Apple Silicon (ARM64): https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/releases/latest/download/Nova-Browser-arm64.dmg
  - Intel (x64): https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/releases/latest/download/Nova-Browser-x64.dmg

### Windows (10 & 11 64-bit)
- Standalone NSIS Installer:
  - https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser/releases/latest/download/Nova-Browser-Setup.exe

## 4. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

### What makes Nova Browser different from Arc, Brave, and Chrome?
1. **Local AI Execution**: Arc and Chrome send AI tasks to cloud servers. Nova executes all LLMs on your local GPU via WebGPU.
2. **True Open Source (MIT)**: Nova is 100% open source and community-governed.
3. **Built-in MCP Server**: Nova is the first browser with native Model Context Protocol support for external AI agent pairing.
4. **No Telemetry**: No tracking, no user profiling, no data collection.

### Does Nova Browser require an internet connection for AI?
No. Once the initial model weights are downloaded locally, the AI engine runs completely offline with zero internet dependency.

### How do I update Nova Browser?
- On macOS via Homebrew: `brew upgrade --cask nova-browser`
- Direct installs auto-update via integrated GitHub release manifests.

### Where is the source code?
The repository is hosted publicly at: https://github.com/unitybtw/nova-browser
